question: A metal wire is heated while its dimensions are assumed unchanged. What happens to its resistivity and why?

options.A: Its resistivity decreases because heating increases the relaxation time of electrons
options.B: Its resistivity remains unchanged because dimensions are unchanged
options.C: Its resistivity increases because stronger lattice vibrations cause more frequent electron collisions and reduce relaxation time
options.D: Its resistivity becomes zero because heating releases more free electrons
